description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between model accuracy metrics and a continuous input variable ranging from approximately 0.71 to 1.00, likely representing a threshold or confidence score. The x-axis is labeled with values at intervals of roughly 0.02, spanning from 0.71 to 1.00, and appears to be on a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, also on a linear scale. Three distinct lines are plotted: “Final Accuracy” (solid blue line with circle markers and error bars) generally trends upward from ~0.90 at x=0.71 to a peak of 1.0 at x=0.79, then fluctuates between 0.85 and 1.0 through x=1.00. “Initial Accuracy” (dashed green line with square markers and error bars) starts at ~0.55 at x=0.71, rises to ~0.90 at x=0.79, dips to ~0.45 at x=0.87, then recovers to ~0.90 by x=1.00. “Δ Accuracy” (dashed orange line with diamond markers and error bars) represents the difference between final and initial accuracy; it begins at ~0.35 at x=0.71, drops sharply to near 0.0 at x=0.73, rises to ~0.30 at x=0.83, then declines again to near 0.0 at x=0.90, with further fluctuations including a peak near 0.40 at x=0.92 before falling to ~0.08 at x=1.00. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability or uncertainty in the measurements.
